newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar president welcomes IMF co-operation.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar president welcomes IMF co-operation.

text.p: Madagascar's interim president and prime minister Norbert Ratsirahonana returned on Sunday from visits to Washington, Paris and Brussels and said he was happy with the progress of moves to unblock IMF and World Bank aid to his country.
Ratsirahonana became interim president when his country's parliament recently impeached president Albert Zafy for allegedly violating the constitution and exceeding his powers.

Ratsirahonana told a press conference in Antananarivo he would consult with his interior minister on Monday on the possible need to postpone the presidential elections due on November 3. He did not elaborate on the reasons for a possible postponement.
Under the present timetable, candidates -- including both Zafy and Ratsirahonana -- would start campaigning on October 13.
Zafy's impeachment in July climaxed three years of political instability after the ousting of former president Didier Ratsiraka following an unprecedented protest campaign.

The political squabbling had frustrated efforts to revive the island republic's economy. But hopes recently rose for the conclusion of agreements with the IMF and the World Bank to reschedule Madagascar's debts and resume lending programmes after a five-year break.

On Sunday Ratsirahonana said the IMF-World Bank negotiations were going well. The IMF was expected to unblock $81.3 million in special drawing rights and the World Bank was expected to release $70 million for structural adjustment.

In Paris, he said, he had discussed the need to revive the Franco-Malgache co-operation commission, and the need for the Paris Club of donors to meet to consider solutions to Madagascar's debt repayment problems.
